notes:
Manuscript page 2 is written at the top and 114 at the lower left. This is a single mathematical manuscript sheet in one hand, without an inscribed date or title. Equation numbers (6)–(10), the three diagonal marginal groups, both formula enclosures, all visible deletions and additions, and the trailing unfinished on le note are retained. Paper folds/edges are not transcribed as drawn ink.

Every token in the original and the two native overlapping halves was compared with both unverified witnesses, including their agreements. Fifteen genuinely open places were then inspected in one saved enlarged crop each. The main reader independently inspected the same fifteen crops and adjudicated several details. No OCR, outside research, or compilation was used. Pure certainty/macro changes are kept in mark decisions rather than inflated into collation rows.

The long underline after (6) starts in the latter part of indiqués and runs under satisfaisant. In (7), ink gives σ_k(r), a left superscript i,j (main adjudication of the detached low mark as comma), a dot, and an open-top three-sided enclosure. The condition begins at/just outside the right edge. In the proche paragraph, the type subscript is literally an oval o, not a restored a; du and R_r^i are baseline text, with only sommet and de r added above them. Their two visible insertion connectors are drawn.

In (8), a distinct extra comma is retained after the source exponent i+1. In (9), the live i precedes the black cancellation, whose residual shape supports +2|i+2 without full resolution. H's live i+1,i is rejected by the ink. The independent finite successor computation below corroborates the resulting active index sequence but was not used to manufacture the reading.

The body says drapeau repère, not disque repéré. The added les a_r^i and its curved connector are reproduced. Cancelled opposé also has a lower underline. The strike through par contre stops before the live les. The raised de = désignent remains tentative, and one small live word above the cancelled sont is retained as sont|des; H's two live words sont des are not supplied. Cancelled tentative une, tentative nous and identités are retained. The plural des sommets was less secure for the first reader but was accepted on the main reader's independent same-crop adjudication.

The first margin note actually says: «On écrit pour simplifier i+1 au lieu du résultat de la permutation circulaire (0,1,∞)↦(1,∞,0), i.e. on identifie {0,1,∞} à Z/3Z…». H incorporates the adjacent equation labels and invents a different successor description. In the second note, désigne is live, the short word after les is cancelled and tentatively ces, and there is no word minuscules.

The lower marginal attachment is genuinely unsettled. In the crop rotated −50° (original box [16,1167,286,1726]), the physical lines are: NB On désigne / par les [cancelled ces?] lettres / les flèches obtenues / après bouchage de / certains trous / si on bouche / R_r^i,. In the next crop, rotated −54° (box [14,1695,252,2030]), a distinct group reads: (NB si / les disques où / λ_r^i devient =1). Both visible si tokens are retained once; the plain R belongs to the first physical group and has no independent overbar. Separate tabular line layouts preserve these groups without collapsing them into C's grammatical reconstructed sentence. This attachment decision uses the existing crops and original-coordinate mapping, as agreed by the main reader; no extra crop was made.

The final NB reads «On supposera que la carte combinatoire se trouve réalisée». The C-like glyph before analytique réelle has an outer C contour and an inner C-like curve, unlike the adjacent plain C in C∞. The ink alone does not securely decide mathbb C versus mathcal C, so both remain. The literal «le découpe de l'éclaté» and «on le note» are retained; the article and noun are not silently regularized to make their genders agree.

The author's preference is retained verbatim as «(Cela [cancelled, tentative nous] semble préférable à la convention de notation inverse)». The three NB notices and «On supposera...» are authored cautions/conventions, not editorial certainty claims. The exact nature and attachment of the lower capping sentence remain unproved. No proof of the global canonical conformal realization or of relations (7) and (10) is asserted.

Two actual mathematical checks were made: a finite successor/endpoint computation for the active (9) arcs, and a local-coordinate check of the boundary/interior assertion for the standard cut (real oriented) blowup. The latter establishes only the local model and does not identify the ambiguous C glyph or decide between possible global conventions for the author's éclaté/découpe.

Main reader inspected two additional crops for D29 and D52. For D04, the existing saved relation7 crop was revisited only because the returned reading contradicted the main prior observation: the detached low mark between i and j is retained as a comma, medium confidence. This is a source reading, not completion from symmetry.

check_events.statement: Locally, the standard cut/real oriented blowup of a real analytic surface at a marked point has a circle boundary and interior equal to the punctured original surface.
check_events.place: final paragraph, surface à bord analytique réelle ... intérieur coïncide avec X\setminus S
check_events.outcome: In a local real analytic chart centred at the point, the model is [0,ε)×S¹ with map (ρ,θ)↦(ρ cosθ,ρ sinθ). Its boundary is {0}×S¹ and its restriction ρ>0 is a real analytic isomorphism to the punctured chart. For analytic changes of centred coordinates with invertible derivative, write the transformed vector as ρ(A(ρ,θ),B(ρ,θ)); A²+B² stays positive near ρ=0, so the new radial variable ρ√(A²+B²) and local angular coordinate are real analytic up to boundary. Thus these local models glue with the claimed boundary/interior property for the standard cut convention. This is not a proof of a global canonical realization or a claim that an uncut projective blowup already has boundary.
